title: Policy Orchestrator and Authorization Middleware for API, Runtime, and Console
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a unified policy orchestration layer ("Policy Orchestrator") and lightweight authorization middleware to enforce RBAC v2 across three surfaces: public API, runtime inference path, and the Redwood Console. The work covers a policy language choice, evaluation engine, decision caching, audit decision logging, role/permission model integrations with SSO/SAML assertions, admin controls, and a staged rollout plan with performance guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Policy Orchestrator implements a stable evaluation API that returns allow/deny with metadata (rule id, reason, matched attributes) within the SLO.

Authorization middleware exists for: 1) API gateway layer, 2) runtime request path (token-to-actor mapping), and 3) console backend routes. Each middleware calls the orchestrator and enforces decisions consistently.
Decision logging: every evaluated decision is emitted to the audit log pipeline with immutable context (actor, token id, resource, action, policy version, matched rule ids).
Integration: SSO/SAML role mappings can be ingested and translated into policy attributes via the sync job; admin-only operations are gated by policies referencing mapped SAML roles.
Performance: end-to-end authorization latency adds no more than 3ms p50 and 10ms p99 for the API middleware when running in production config, verified by benchmarks under median traffic patterns.
Canary deployment validates correctness and no functional regressions for 72 hours at 5% traffic before 25% and then full rollout.
Automated unit and integration tests cover positive/negative rules, caching invalidation, multi-tenant isolation, and fallback behavior.
Documentation and runbook published: Confluence design doc, migration checklist for existing roles, and incident playbook for authorization failures.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Core evaluator prototype (Rego-backed PoC) + API middleware stub. Phase 2: Harden evaluator, add decision caching and versioned policies, add audit logging hooks and schema. Phase 3: Runtime middleware integration (low-latency path), console middleware, SSO mapping sync job, e2e tests and canary rollout. Phase 4: Observability, tracing, perf tuning, and policy authoring UX. Each phase will have a dedicated PR and migration runbook.
design_decisions: Policy language: Rego (Open Policy Agent) preferred for expressiveness and community tools; evaluate custom lightweight AST if p99 latency cannot be achieved.
Evaluation model: centralized policy orchestrator service with local read-only caches in each surface to meet latency SLOs and enable consistent policy versioning.

Audit logging: decision-level logs will be immutable, append-only, and include policy_version and matched_rule_ids; logs will be forwarded to our existing audit pipeline (Kafka -> ClickHouse / S3 archive).
SSO mapping: SAML role assertions will be mapped to internal role_ids by a nightly sync job with manual overrides stored in admin Console.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: OPA Rego evaluation may be too slow on the hot inference path. Mitigation: precompile common queries, run in-process WASM in runtime path, fall back to a simple allowlist TTL cache.
Risk: Inconsistent enforcement between surfaces. Mitigation: single evaluation API and integration tests asserting identical decisions for canonical request vectors.
Risk: Audit logs overload storage. Mitigation: sample low-risk read-only decisions by default, full logging for admin and write operations, and configurable retention per customer tier.
Risk: Mis-mapped SAML roles granting admin access accidentally. Mitigation: require owner approval for new admin mappings and send alert to security queue on mapping changes.
qa_plan: Unit tests for evaluator logic and policy parsing. Integration tests exercising API -> orchestrator -> decision log pipeline. Load tests for middleware latency under realistic token and model request mixes. Staged canary with traffic shaping and 24/7 on-call during rollout window.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy orchestrator v0 to internal env; 2) Deploy API middleware that delegates to orchestrator for 5% of traffic; 3) Monitor metrics for 72h; 4) Expand to 25% if no regressions; 5) Add runtime middleware in controlled clusters; 6) Flip console routes after backend and RBAC authoring UX is enabled; 7) Run migration script to update policy versions and notify customers.
